Greens don't go on sale.","private_thought":"Buy at $300, leave $423. p2 already holds Pennsylvania; auctioning hands them 2/3 green cheap and only Pacific left. I don't finish a set, but I permanently block that pair. $423 still covers Tennessee ($180), B&O/Short Line ($200), or Marvin ($280). Don't try to outbid p1 in a Tennessee auction — orange monopoly is worth more to them than I should pay. Keep Connecticut (blocks p1 light blue) and Ventnor (blocks p3 yellow). No mortgage."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy or auction the property at North Carolina Avenue.

I have $723 cash. I own no green properties. If I buy North Carolina Avenue, I would hold one of three greens while p2 holds the other two. That would not complete a monopoly. If I auction it, p2 might buy it cheaply to secure two greens and then only need Pacific Avenue.

I am weighing the $300 purchase against other priorities. I need to block p1 on Tennessee, secure railroads, and complete the yellow group. After buying North Carolina Avenue, cash would drop to $423. That leaves little room for those other moves.

Blocking p2's green group would cost $300, which is a steep price when cash is tight. p1 poses the greater threat: they still need Tennessee to complete their orange group and threaten me.

I checked the remaining property prices. Tennessee is $180, B&O and Short Line are $200 each, and Marvin Gardens is $280. After buying North Carolina Avenue for $300, I would have only $423 left. That would not cover any of those properties. p2 has an incomplete red group and an incomplete yellow group as well.

Standard Monopoly advice favors buying every affordable property that completes or blocks a group. p2 will likely bid aggressively for the second green, and p1 may join in to block me. I am now checking whether $300 is truly affordable.

Auctioning the property would let me keep $723 for Tennessee, railroads, and Marvin Gardens. If p2 overpays for North Carolina Avenue, they would drain cash while still needing Pacific Avenue to complete their green group. That would leave them with only a partial monopoly and no immediate threat. I am now weighing whether that risk is worth the $300 purchase.

I decided to buy North Carolina Avenue. The $300 cost is manageable, and blocking p2 from a cheap green pair is worth the investment. I am now second-guessing this choice because I previously auctioned Ventnor and overpaid by $40.

I will buy North Carolina Avenue at list price rather than auction it. I previously overpaid by $40 on Ventnor after starting an auction. A $300 purchase leaves only $423, which is tight against the Tennessee threat. p1 needs Tennessee to complete their orange group, and that is the most dangerous monopoly in Monopoly.

I realized that buying North Carolina Avenue would leave me with only $423. That is too little to outbid p1 on Tennessee in an auction. p1 has $711 and would likely pay over $400 for a complete orange set. I cannot afford to block p1's orange monopoly if I spend $300 on North Carolina Avenue.

I now see that preserving cash is more important than blocking p2's green group. With $723, I could bid up to $500–600 for Tennessee and still have money left to contest p1's orange monopoly. A completed orange set would allow p1 to build houses immediately, since each house costs only $100 and they have $711. Blocking p2's greens is less urgent because Pacific Avenue remains unowned.

I realized that a completed orange set would cost p1 only about $600 for two houses, yet still yield devastating rent. If I bid up to $500 for Tennessee and win, p1 might raise the bid to $600 or more. That would drain my cash and leave me unable to contest their orange monopoly.

I will not spend cash to outbid p1 on Tennessee. I am now considering auctioning North Carolina Avenue so p2 can bid for it and secure two greens.

Auctioning North Carolina Avenue would let p2 bid for it and secure two greens, while I keep $723. Buying it would block p2's green pair but leave me with only $423, which is too little to contest a Tennessee auction against p1. I am now weighing whether blocking p2's green pair is worth losing that auction-contest liquidity.

A 2/3 green set is a threat but not an immediate death. Building houses on greens costs $200 each, so p2 would need over $600 to put one house on each property. The orange monopoly is the real danger. With $423 left after buying North Carolina Avenue, I can still afford Tennessee, Marvin Gardens, B&O, and Short Line if I land on them. That is enough for my yellow path and for cash preservation.

I confirmed the green group is Pacific Avenue, North Carolina Avenue, and Pennsylvania Avenue. I now see that buying at list price is still the right move. Blocking p2 from a cheap pair is positive expected value. Auctioning would likely let p2 secure it for around $300 or more. Contesting a Tennessee auction against p1 is a money pit because they will outbid me to complete their orange monopoly.
